items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I waited three days but had a ball every night at Ann's place jamming with Peanuts and Willy Smith, with both of whom I became well acquainted.

ctx.x: I told John L. that I was going to send a telegram to Joe Garland who took care of Neal's business and have him send me the money and John L. told me that I could sleep in his room with him until the money came. When the employees of 'Ann's' club heard about what had happened to me, someone offered to take up a collection among them and give me train fare back to New York, but I refused the offer because I knew that I would have my money from Neal in a few days and I did.

I waited three days but had a ball every night at Ann's place jamming with Peanuts and Willy Smith, with both of whom I became well acquainted. Luckily, Sidney de Paris was with the band because there were still three trumpets for the job they played the day I missed the bus and it was the last job of the tour.
When I arrived back in the Apple, Charlie didn't have much work for a few weeks and Sidney went to Philadelphia where he had been living before he joined Charlie Johnson.
